How do healthcare systems compare?

Compare access, affordability and outcomes in the Commonwealth Fund’s 2024 study, with a separate OECD comparison for Poland.

Which healthcare systems perform best?

Mirror, Mirror 2024 compared patient experiences and health-system performance in ten wealthy countries. Australia, the Netherlands and the UK placed highest overall. If your priority is getting timely care you can afford, the Netherlands is a particularly useful example.

Netherlands

Regulated insurers offer compulsory basic coverage. A family doctor usually coordinates care. The country performed well on both availability and affordability.

Australia

Medicare provides free hospital treatment for public patients in public hospitals and covers some or all of the cost of doctor visits. Australia ranked first overall.

United Kingdom

The tax-funded NHS provides most services free at the point of care. This protects patients against large bills, though waits for some planned procedures can be long.

Germany

Germany’s social insurance system joined the Netherlands near the top for both availability and affordability.

US and Poland

The US ranked last among the ten. Poland was outside the study. A separate 2025 OECD report recorded 114 deaths from treatable causes per 100,000 people in Poland, compared with an OECD average of 77. This measure covers causes for which timely and effective healthcare can usually avert death before age 75.
